content:
deploy-bot: starting canary traffic shift to GREEN in region-west -> 20% at t=1977654321

maya: saw the alert — 5xx rate jumped in west canary shortly after the shift :eyes:

incident-bot: paging maya for SEV-2 (canary errors in region-west) :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it. pulling graphs now (dash link: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/abcd1234)

alex: noted. any customer  impact so far?

maya: app-errors spike ~2.4% -> 8% for west, p95 latency +300ms. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Errors are mostly 502/504 from gateway.

luis: looks like a routing mismatch on the edge — some edge proxies still sending to BLUE by name but headers expect GREEN variant (model id mismatch). Seen this before with stale NGINX map caches.

maya: can you show the proxy logs?

luis: grabbing tail:```
edge-proxy-12 | GET /v1/generate 200ms -> upstream 502 
upstream hint: route=green-variant-v2, host=blue-inference-west-01.internal
```

sam: that explains cross-region/blue-green mismatch — weight flip changed control plane but some host mappings didn't refresh. TTLs look low but we still have in-memory routing maps.

jessica: customers are starting to DM support — small cluster of enterprise customers in EU-WEST routed via west edges hitting it. Not yet large but trending.

maya: mitigation options: 1) kill the canary (set route weight back to BLUE=100%), 2) force edge config sync, 3) rollback the deployment itself. Prefer quickest low-risk: kill canary weight and let caches drain.

alex: agree. execute kill-switch on rollout policy and flip traffic back to BLUE. Who has console access?

maya: me. doing `redwoodctl rollout set-weight --region west --green 0` now.

deploy-bot: received command, applying weight change...

deploy-bot: weight update complete: green=0%, blue=100%

maya: pushing `edge-config reload` to all west proxies to flush in-memory maps (rolling):
```bash
for node in $(list-west-edge); do ssh $node 'systemctl restart edge-proxy' & done
```

luis: restarting nodes slowly, starting with low-traffic ones. I'll watch 502 count.

incident-bot: note: attenuating alerts to pagers while mitigation in progress. DM if escalations.

maya: after weight flip + rolling reload: errors down to 0.9% and p95 near baseline. Latency normalizing.

sam: customer reports trickling down. No open high-severity tickets.

jessica: logging: which customers were hit? I can trigger outreach if needed.

maya: internal query shows traffic from account IDs: acct_17, acct_42, acct_88. Small volume retail and 1 enterprise sandbox. No paid customers in hard failure.

alex: root cause hypothesis: control-plane race — rollout service updated traffic weights before edge mapping service finished propagating green host mappings; short window where host header -> blue backend mismatch -> 502. Repro steps nailed locally.

luis: filed a short-term fix: block weight flips until edge-config and dns caches report 'ok' from propagation checker. Will open PR to rollout controller.

maya: creating incident ticket INC-1977654321 with timeline and mitigation notes.

sam: handoff — I need to leave in 15. maya, can you stay until postmortem draft? alex will cover oncall after 20:30.

maya: will stay. alex, you good to take final sign-off?

alex: yep. I'll remain watch for 30m then close.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Next step: postmortem. Assigning owners: RCA=luis, mitigation=maya, outreach=jessica.

maya: quick follow-up action items: 
- rollback-controller: add propagation gating (luis)
- enhance observability: add metric `edge-mapping-stale_count` (alex)
- run-game: rehearse region-weight flip (eng-sre)

jessica: I'll message affected customers with timeline + reassure.

maya: handing off to alex now for quiet watch. leaving channel for handoff +1. :white_check_mark:

alex: acknowledged. I'll close thread when green for 30m. Thanks all for quick triage.
